reason: The copied instructions and amino acids are the ingredients the repair cell needs to make collagen.
expectation: The cell will use the instructions and amino acids to make collagen.

effect: The repair cell made collagen chains from the amino acids; the picture shows the RNA template remains intact. The chains still need delivery outside the cell.
reaction: The distinction between making the chains and delivering them is clear.
reason: The Golgi and vesicles are pictured carrying material toward the cell boundary, so they appear to be the next step in delivering the collagen.
expectation: The Golgi and vesicles will process and carry the collagen toward the cell boundary for release.

effect: The collagen has been released and assembled into supporting fibers outside the cell, completing the first goal. The fibers can now help rebuild the wound.
reaction: The sequence from protein production to support outside the cell is clear.
reason: The new supporting fibers appear suited to replacing the missing support beneath the scrape.
expectation: The fibers will replace some of the missing support beneath the wound.

effect: The new fibers filled the deeper gap, but the surface cells have not yet closed the scrape.
reaction: The picture makes the remaining gap clear.
reason: The local repair signals are shown reaching skin cells at the wound edge, so they may prompt those cells to close the gap.

choice.with: Skin cells at the scrape’s edge

expectation: The signals will prompt the edge cells to move across the gap.

effect: The signals prompted the edge cells to divide and crawl toward the gap. They can now be added to the rebuilding body.
reaction: The dividing and crawling cells make the repair process easier to follow.
reason: The spreading surface cells appear to be the remaining piece needed to close the scrape.
expectation: The surface cells will cover the gap above the new supporting fibers.

effect: The surface gap is closed, while the deeper collagen continues remodeling. Both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The distinction between a closed surface and continuing deeper repair was helpful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making and releasing collagen was the most worthwhile sequence. It connected protein production inside a cell to the support fibers that help repair tissue outside it.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the finished fibers to the body was fairly predictable, though the result clearly showed that the surface gap remained.

surprise.text: I was interested that the surface could close while the deeper collagen was still loosely arranged and remodeling continued.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the item descriptions and results gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue if another chapter explored a different body process. This one made the link between cell work and tissue repair clear, though several combinations were predictable.
